standard_prerequisites.name: Tor dimension of objects of the derived category can be computed at stalks, by the cohomology tor amplitude stalk lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces part (1) to a stalkwise computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a tor independent cartesian square the derived pullback stalk identifies with the derived tensor product over the base ring, by the More on Algebra base change comparison lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the stalk of L(g')^*E as a tensor over O_{S,s}.

standard_prerequisites.name: For modules over rings, tor amplitude is preserved under derived tensor with a ring of tor amplitude in degree zero, by the More on Algebra pull tor amplitude lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes part (1); part (2) follows by reading flatness as tor amplitude in [0, 0].

core_obligations: Stalkwise setup: tor dimension is computed at stalks; for x' over x the stalk of L(g')^*E is E_x tensor^L O_{X',x'} (proof lines 5533-5538).

Use tor independence of X and S' over S and the base change comparison lemma to identify this with E_x tensor^L_{O_{S,s}} O_{S',s'}; the pull tor amplitude lemma then shows the stalk has tor amplitude in [a, b] over f'^{-1}O_{S'}, giving part (1) (proof lines 5539-5547).
Part (2): flatness of G over S means G[0] has tor amplitude in [0, 0] as a complex of f^{-1}O_S-modules; applying part (1) gives L(g')^*G = (g')^*G (proof lines 5548-5550).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the stalk via tor independence and conclude part (1) (proof lines 5539-5547).
Deduce part (2) from part (1) by the degree-zero tor amplitude reading of flatness (proof lines 5548-5550).
